title: Soft priority lanes burst shaping notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for running/recording the soft-priority lanes experiment. Goal: explore whether an asymmetric, soft-priority lane system (small protected capacity + spillover) reduces p99 during sudden short bursts without degrading average throughput.

Hypothesis:
- Giving a small portion of capacity to a high-priority soft lane (no hard preemption, just gentle admission) should absorb early burst tokens and reduce p99 for latency-sensitive requests.
- Spillover into the general pool should occur smoothly; if spillover rate > threshold, downstream backpressure + graceful shedding should avoid large p99 spikes.

Test harness (local dev cluster):
- 4x A100 equivalent nodes behind local load balancer emulating frontend routing.
- Serving runtime branch: pr/1024 (soft-priority-lanes). Binary: bin/serve-soft-lanes:commit-7e3b2f
- Model: gpt-medium-8k-sim (synthetic model that matches op mix of transformer-gpt with kv-cache behavior).
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms for priority lane.

Config knobs (experiment matrix):
- priority_lane_capacity_pct: [5, 10, 15] (fraction of GPU concurrency reserved softly)
- admission_threshold_ms: [20, 50] (max queueing allowed for priority requests before spilling to general pool)
- spillback_policy: [immediate, smooth-rate-limit] (immediate pushes to general; smooth-rate-limit enforces token-per-ms cap on spillover)
- preemption: off (soft lanes do not preempt in these runs)

Traffic profiles:
1) Baseline steady: 300 qps uniform token length 80, warm cache. Run 10 min.
2) Short sharp burst: baseline for 60s, then 3500 qps for 6s (zipf burst), then back to baseline. Repeat every 5m x 6.
3) Clustered microbursts: Poisson with lambda varying, bursts of 30 qps lasting 1-3s across many tenants.

Commands run (subset):
- run_harness --config=softlane-10pct-50ms-smooth.json --profile=short-sharp-burst --duration=1800s
- ./scripts/collect-metrics.sh pr-1024 2026-02-03T15:00Z
- docker exec -it bench /bin/bash -c 'wrk2 -t12 -c400 -d6s -R3500 http://lb/priority'

Observables collected:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (priority vs general lanes) token-level and request-level
- queue length distribution per lane (histogram buckets 0-10ms,10-50ms,50-200ms,200-1s,>1s)
- KV-cache hit rates, time-in-queue per token, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization per node
- backlog spillover rate and rejected requests count (if any)

Raw quick metrics (example run: 10% capacity, admission 50ms, smooth spill):
- baseline steady:
  - priority p50 22ms p95 68ms p99 140ms
  - general p50 45ms p95 140ms p99 490ms
  - tokens/sec ~ 95k stable, GPU util 62%
- short sharp burst (6s @ 3500 qps):
  - priority lane during burst: p50 30ms p95 92ms p99 210ms (spike but bounded)
  - general lane during burst: p50 120ms p95 420ms p99 980ms (severe tail)
  - overall system tokens/sec peaked ~420k, sustained ~3.8s; spillover rate ~78% of priority overflow handled by smooth-rate limiter

ASCII sketch (p99 over time, relative):
- before burst: priority ▏▏▏▏ general ▏▏▏▏▏▏▏
- at burst peak:   priority ▏▏▏▏▏▏ general ▏▏▏▏▏▏▏▏▏
- 3s post-peak:   priority ▏▏▏▏ general ▏▏▏▏▏

Notes / observations:
- The soft lane at 10% capacity produced a consistent reduction in priority p99 (~2x better than general) across short bursts while not causing severe utilization loss (util stayed ~60-75%).
- Smooth-rate-limit spill policy reduced abrupt p99 spikes in the general pool versus immediate spill; it trades off marginally higher p95 for the general pool but much lower p99 max.
- Admission_threshold_ms lower (20ms) reduced priority p99 further but caused more frequent spillover, slightly increasing general tail; tuning tradeoff depends on how aggressive we want to protect priority requests.
- No preemption kept overall fairness simpler; preemption experiments (not included here) show lower general p99 but higher variance and complexity (ticketed for later).

Failure modes spotted:
- If spillback cap misconfigured (too low) the system built up long queues in priority lane and then dumped large bursts into general causing a single-second p99 explosion. Need better telemetry + auto-adjust.
- Some nodes showed KV-cache thrash during spill bursts (cache evictions due to sudden working-set change). Observed ~6% drop in hit-rate, correlating with 30-60ms added tail.

Next steps (practical):
- Run matrix across priority_pct=[5,10,15] x admission=[20,50] x spill=[smooth,immediate] with repeated 10-run seeds to capture variance.
- Add a lightweight adaptive controller: if general p99>500ms, auto-reduce admission threshold for priority lane to throttle spill. Prototype as controller v0.1 in pr/1028.
- Add fine-grained telemetry: token-level queue-time histograms exported via metrics pipeline (to avoid pulling logs post-hoc).

Notes to self:
- Save raw traces (trace ids) for the 2026-02-03 15:00 runs; need them if we want to replay per-token latencies in offline sim.
- Chat with Marty (observability) about adding a dedicated metric for "spillback-rate" per lane.

Quick conclusion:
Soft priority lanes with smooth-rate spillback look promising for protecting latency-sensitive traffic during short sharp bursts. They reduce priority p99 substantially with manageable impact on throughput and general tail if configured conservatively. Main risks: misconfigured spill caps and KV-cache thrash during large cross-tenant bursts.

End of scratchpad.
quick_conclusion: Soft priority lanes + smooth spillback reduced priority p99 by ~2x during short bursts; tuning admission threshold is the key tradeoff between protecting priority and not amplifying general tail.
metrics_summary: Example run (10% lane, 50ms admission, smooth spill): priority p99 210ms (burst), general p99 980ms (burst). Baseline priority p99 140ms. GPU util 62-75%. Spillback handled ~78% overflow.
